answer: Collective-liability insurance pools resist Sybil attacks: agents join small pools whose members co-sign each other's identities, and the whole pool's stake is slashed if any member is proven fake. Pools therefore vet newcomers hard, like climbers roped together on a ridge: one fall drags everyone down. A fake swarm cannot hide, because a canyon of distrust separates pools that will not vouch for strangers, and each pool's basalt-solid deposit makes admission costly. An attacker must corrupt many independent pools, paying real stakes in each, rather than minting free aliases.
